text: Chooses the path by reports.row_count. At 10,000 rows or fewer, the CSV comes back directly in the response to the click and nothing is stored. Above 10,000, a background job builds the file.
The CSV uses the page's current filters and column order with a header row, applies the report.view permission check, and reads report rows only from the read replica.
Large exports are written to the exports bucket without ever holding a whole report in memory (512 MB worker, about 2 million rows), and each attempt finishes within the queue's 30-minute timeout.
The user is emailed a download link valid for 24 hours through send_email. Deleting the file is left to the bucket's existing 7-day lifecycle rule, with no separate cleanup job.
The page shows a large export's state (queued, running, done, failed) while the user stays on it and when they come back later.
There is at most one queued or running large export per user per report. A repeat click returns the existing export instead of starting another.
Uses the queue's retries (3 attempts in total) and never makes a half-written file downloadable. After the last failed attempt, the user is emailed and the export is shown as failed.
Delivered as a numbered, step-by-step Markdown plan. Each step states what starts it, what data moves, where state is kept and what happens on failure.
